issue.description:
Plan: docs/plan/plan.md revision 10, transition ledger BR-T12 ("Attribution"). Independent of the
attempt-outcome tranche BR-T03..T08; relates to the epic beadrs-f428fcfd. Consumer: NEEDLE needle-c81694f1.

## Why
`service::issues` already takes an optional actor and defaults to `"system"` (src/service/issues.rs
~L259); only the CLI never passes one, except on claim. Every `closed`, `released`, `updated` and
`reopened` event in `.beads/checkpoint/forensic.jsonl` therefore reads actor `system`, which makes
closure unattributable for git-activity-exporter and for the NEEDLE attempt ledger.

## Task
- Add `--actor <ACTOR>` to `close`, `release`, `reopen`, `update`, `claim`, `dep add|remove`,
  `label add|remove`, `comments add`; precedence flag > `BEAD_ACTOR` env > `"system"`.
- Thread it to the service layer so the audit/forensic event's `actor` is the caller identity;
  no new event kinds, no schema-breaking change (additive to `native-v1`).
- `bead capabilities` (and the `needle-v1` profile snapshot) advertise `actor_on_mutations: true` so
  consumers can detect support without parsing help text.
- Docs: one paragraph in the CLI reference and in the checkpoint/forensic schema note.

## Acceptance
- Forensic fixtures show the given actor on `closed`, `released`, `reopened`, `updated`.
- Without flag or env the output is byte-identical to today (`system`).
- Old checkpoints import unchanged; old clients ignore the added capability key.
- fmt, clippy, tests, installed-binary help test pass at the release commit.
issue.title: Accept --actor and BEAD_ACTOR on every mutating command and record it in the audit event (BR-T12)

issue.description:
ADR-003 records that the sharded writer is content-addressed but unreachable because `cmd_sync_flush_only` hardcodes `CheckpointMode::Monolithic`, and that flush cost is linear in workspace size because `publish_forensic_checkpoint` re-reads and re-serializes everything on each call. The open remediation beads (content-address the monolithic root object; apply pointer-declared tombstones) fix monolithic-mode growth but not the linear per-mutation wall-time, and nothing tracks exposing sharded/incremental publication. Remove the hardcoded mode, add explicit checkpoint-mode selection (config and/or CLI), keep `sync status` and `restore` correct across both modes (forensic.jsonl is retired in sharded mode per beadrs-43d4bcb6), and add conformance for generation round-trip and restore-into-empty in sharded mode plus a measurement showing per-mutation flush cost no longer scales with total workspace size.

---
Priority: P2
Created by: weave strand
issue.title: Make sharded checkpoint mode reachable instead of hardcoded Monolithic in sync flush
